#758. Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro (second left) is shown a red card by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.

"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.

"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.

"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"

United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.

They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.

It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.

'And the three points?' - Pochettino after Yoro red overturned

Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.

There has been no apology from Webb on this occasion.

Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball."

United sources claim this interpretation is wrong.

The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.

This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.

Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.

"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.

"We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?"

What referee's chief Webb said about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.

"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.

"That if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong."

United's fury over Yoro and the way the situation has been handled cannot completely obscure the fact they lost 4-0 in Pochettino's first game in charge.

It extended a terrible start to the season that has seen the Red Devils win on just three occasions - and only once in the Premier League, against newly-promoted Ipswich in August.

The club are 19th in the Premier League and facing up to the possibility of being relegated for the first time since 1973-74.

Yet Pochettino is adamant there is no fragility about his new squad.

"The situation is fragile in [terms of] the environment, or the people want it to look like we're fragile. But I don't say that we are fragile. I think we are strong.

"We have great mentality and a great mindset.

"There are many things we need to improve. It's normal to be in a different position, and everyone can use different words to describe the situation.

"But we are a strong team. They showed that last season, capable of finishing third. I think we are going to turn around the situation and start to perform in the level like before Bruno [Fernandes] said, deserve to be at this club."

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (left) and skipper Bruno Fernandes speak to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Sporting in Lisbon

Skipper Bruno Fernandes revealed at the weekend talks over a new United contract were on hold.

The 32-year-old's present deal expires in the summer, although the club have an option to extend it by 12 months.

Speaking alongside Pochettino at a media conference before his first meeting with Sporting since he left to join United in a Â£47m deal in January 2020, Fernandes said his sole focus at present is to drag United out of the mire.

"For us to start winning games, then we can start speaking about contract," he said.

"It's not important now. It's irrelevant. Obviously, I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look into that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that.

"I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment."

#757. Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find new forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

Countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," said Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

She says it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it shows it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels."

She says it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF plans and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott said.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national plans to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no new commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Kumar says more countries could announce similar plans just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

The nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

The roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

Kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any big announcements about fossil fuels.

Global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald shows that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing new reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

One issue Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar said, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum."

#756. Transform Your Boyfriend Into a Heartthrob This Holiday Season

Just because you date men doesn't mean you have to suffer. Consider these skincare, hair, and fragrance items as gifts for him and as a beautifully packaged favor for yourself ahead of the holidays.

Don't you wish your boyfriend was hot? While hot men have always been popular, there's a real resurgence of the heartthrob happening recently. Whether it's the Heated Rivalry boys or another actor that the internet has deemed their favorite hottie of the month, we're not just obsessed with their looks anymore... we want to know their hair, skin, and grooming secrets.

People are buying everything that celebrity groomers are using to prep their heartthrob clients (think Aika Flores and her roster of clients like Hudson Williams, Belmont Cameli, and Joe Jonas).

Why? In the hopes of transforming their ugly boyfriends into hotties, of course. Now... don't yell at me for calling your man ugly; I find almost all men ugly (except for Flores' clients, apparently).

Flores has become known for bringing back the heartthrob hair and skin to the fandom-obsessed Hollywood that we saw with boy groups during the early 00s, that has us genuinely curious about the products they're using to get the look.

With so many grooming products out there (and more launching all the time), how do you know what to give your boyfriend? It seems like the secret could actually be a lesbian's touch. Flores and I are both lesbians... Coincidence? I think not! So, let me be your unbiased guide in this gifting journey ahead of the holidays.

Of course, I can't promise to fix your dating-men symptoms! But together, we can at least get him to look better... not for him, but for you. You're welcome!

If your man doesn't have the same head of hair that he used to have once upon a time, Toppik is the product he needs. New growth can take months (if not years), so these weather-resistant hair fibers (made of colored keratin protein) blend seamlessly with existing hair to instantly create a fuller appearance while you wait.

This serum is specifically formulated for men with Ashwagandha Exosomes to replenish all the nutrients the scalp needs directly. It supports visibly thicker and stronger-feeling hair while improving visible density and being completely lightweight.

You need to give your boyfriend a separate shampoo and conditioner; none of that 2-in-1 nonsense. Pick the perfect shampoo according to his scalp type, but in general, Nutrire's S.2 Shampoo is a safe (and perfect) choice for most scalps. It promises to wash his scalp of everything without drying it out.

Pick the perfect conditioner, according to your man's strand type. If he's somewhere between fine and thick hair, this conditioner is ideal. Its formula is infused with prickly pear extract, sunflower seed oil, and shea butter to hydrate and prevent breakage for glossy locks.

For his skin, he has to establish an excellent cleansing routine—because let's face it, he probably hasn't washed his face in...well, never. If you're looking for a good one, we recommend this SKIN1004 set that includes the brand's cleansing oil and foam cleanser. Plus, if the brand's ambassador, Hudson Williams, believes in double cleansing, so do we—although he uses this foaming cleanser instead, alongside the oil!

Don't forget the eyes! While there are plenty of eye creams out there, this e.l.f. SKIN one is surprisingly hydrating for its affordable price, with its quick-absorbing formula of hyaluronic acid and peptides to lock in moisture without irritating even the most sensitive eyes.

If your man has dry skin (especially during the winter), this LANEIGE sleeping mask is like an extremely hydrating, depuffing, and cooling dream come true. While technically an overnight treatment that's meant to wash off in the morning, I use it as a moisturizer that my skin absorbs without any stickiness.

Don't let your man walk around with crusty, disgusting lips! We beg! If not for us, then for you! You have to kiss all of that. Get him a clear lip balm and treatment in a scent that won't scare him away, like this Summer Fridays one in Sweet Mint.

No matter how many skincare products or devices you use, it won't mean anything if you're not drinking enough water. And that's true of your boyfriend too! Make his water intake easier to manage with this cool Stanley tumbler in a Dried Pine design that has a handy built-in straw that flips up.

Most people have redness and inflammation in their skin, and boyfriends are no exception. It's incredible how much of a difference a good LED light face mask can make! This one from RENPHO features a cordless design, a silicone sculpt that contours his face, and five light modes (red, blue, and near-infrared) to target different skin conditions.

Your man has to smell good, but without giving you a headache. The secret isn't a stronger scent; it's a light one that he can easily layer. The Salt & Stone body mist in the scent Santal & Vetiver is perfect for that, with its woody and sexy notes of Australian sandalwood, amber, orris, ambrox, cedar, violet leaves, vetiver, and crystal.

You also want him to have some fun with his fragrances! Add a little magic and storytelling to his scents with Heretic Parfum. If he's a film buff (and excited about Robert Eggers' upcoming Werwulf film), he'll be blown away by this new limited-edition fragrance that's described as seductive, mysterious, and animalistic.

Want something a little more gourmand and less earthy while still being manly? This cologne from DIME has a clean and charming scent with notes of fresh lime, sparkling grapefruit, dark rum, blue lavender, rosemary sprig, crushed cardamom, tonka bean, amber woods, and leather.

#752. DWTS’ Ezra Frech Gives Dating Life Update Amid Hailey Bills Rumors

Dancing With the Stars finalist Ezra Frech said he's "not necessarily looking for a relationship" amid dating rumors with pro dancer Hailey Bills: "It’ll probably stay that way for a while."

Ezra Frech isn't looking for a partner outside of the Dancing With the Stars ballroom at the moment.

The Paralympian shared an update on his dating life amid romance rumors surrounding himself and DWTS pro dancer Hailey Bills, calling the online chatter "crazy."

"Right now, I’m definitely single but not necessarily looking for a relationship," Frech emphasized in an interview with Cosmopolitan published Nov. 23. "Because, again, once the dance season ends, I’ll be committing myself entirely to track again."

He added, "I’m enjoying being single, and it’ll probably stay that way for a while."

But that's not to say the two will shimmy on their separate ways when season 35 of the ABC dance competition series ends Nov. 24. As Frech put it, "I could see myself still talking to pretty much everybody on the cast."

"Amber [Glenn] is someone who is a real close part of my life and will be for a long time," the 21-year-old said, adding that he's also developed a friendship with his dance partner Daniella Karagach and her husband, fellow pro Pasha Pashkov. "Guillermo [Rodriguez] is someone I’m going to be close to forever. Me, him and Connor [Wood]—we’re in the group chat texting all the time."

Still, parting is such sweet sorrow for Frech, who was one of the celebrity finalists alongside Glenn, Wood, Maura Higgins and Tatyana Ali.

"I’ll miss getting to see everyone at the rehearsal studio," he said. "I’ll miss getting the opportunity to commit myself to something like this so entirely. And I’m gonna miss the show days."

"You become so close to everybody, and you spend so much time around these people, and then all of a sudden, it’s going to end," Frech added. "But the good thing is that these people are still going to be in my life."

As for Bills' thoughts on the romance rumors? The 20-year-old—who competed alongside Sarah Jane Nader before being eliminated during the September premiere—quipped on DWTS' Nov. 2 episode, “Oh, I would love to see Ezra Frech.”

However, Frech admitted at the time that he only had eyes for the Mirrorball Trophy.

“I’m locked in on dancing right now,” he shared. “That’s all I’ll say.”

While Frech and Bills are dancing on their own, read on for other celebs who found love on DWTS.

The season 33 partners dated for about seven months between 2024 and spring 2025.

In April 2025, the fellow DWTS pros kissed on the lips onstage on the final night of the series' 2025 tour during their show-closing duet dance, confirming months of romance rumors.

Months after placing fifth in the 31st season of the dance show, the couple confirmed their romance on Valentine's Day 2023. "My Valentine," the CODA actor captioned a selfie with the choreographer. "Happy Valentine's Day!"

Stewart and Durant then announced their engagement in December 2023 and married in front of a trouple of DWTS pros in August 2025.

While she was partnered with Hayes Grier, the two hit it off during season 21's Switch Up Week, with Skarlatos calling the pro dancer "so hot." After her elimination, Slater teased that they two had yet to go on a date, saying, "We'll see."

Meanwhile, Skarlatos playfully told E! News, "No comment!"

The dance pro and Bachelorette alum were romantically linked while competing together on DWTS' season 33 in 2024. However, their offscreen chemistry fizzled out by June 2025 shortly after Tran returned to Miami to finish her master's degree.

Which bring us to these two. After dating a little on-and-off since 2011, the pros got engaged live on the show in October 2016 and were married in March 2018. However, E! News confirmed in August 2022 that Slater and Farber were going their separate ways after four years of marriage.

"It's not a nightmare at all," Slater told E! News. "We support each other so much that I want the very best for Sasha. We support each other, very, very truly."

Chmerkovskiy and Johnson were dating in 2015, before she was promoted to pro dancer. They got engaged in June of 2018 before making it official and walking down the aisle in April of 2019. The two welcomed son Rome Valentin in January 2023.

"Life is awesome," Chmerkovskiy told E! News in May 2023. Becoming a dad "definitely elevated my joy for life, my joy for my family, and every day I learn something new being a father."

In December 2020, E! News learned the Selling Sunset star was dating the Dancing With the Stars pro after they had competed separately on season 29.

However, after two months of dating, E! News exclusively confirmed they had called it quits. At the time, a source close to the realtor said, "They had a fun time together but in the end, decided it would be best if they part ways. They are still friendly and cordial. It wasn't a messy breakup, just wasn't the right fit or right timing."

Platonic throughout their seventh-place-finishing 2017 run, the Total Bellas star and the former Dancing With the Stars pro found their way back to each other after her split from John Cena in 2018. Garcia confirmed her relationship with Chigvintsev in May 2019, and they got engaged later that year.

The WWE Hall of Famer learned she was expecting soon after their Paris engagement, with them welcoming son Matteo Artemovich Chigvintsev in 2020.

Sadly, though, the pair are no longer partnering up. Garcia filed for divorce in September 2024, two weeks after Chigvintsev was arrested on suspicion of domestic violence. Ultimately, the Napa County District Attorney's office announced they decided not to file charges against him "after a thorough review of the criminal investigation and careful evaluation of the evidence presented to the DA’s Office."

The pair settled their divorce in November 2024, with Garcia's rep noting the two also dropped their "the domestic violence restraining orders against each other in an effort to move on with their lives and effectively co-parent their son."

The model and the relatively new pro flirted up a storm throughout season 27, and Ren had admitted on the show that she had a crush on him. At the time, a source even told E! News that they "really enjoy each other's company" and were "seeing where things go."

However, multiple outlets reported in December 2018 that the pair had split.

The professional dancers got engaged on Dec. 5, 2015, after dating since 2012. Maks proposed onstage at the SWAY: A Dance Trilogy event in Miami. Six months after welcoming their son Shai, the lovebirds exchanged vows during a lavish ceremony in July 2017. They then welcomed baby Rio in June 2023 and their third son Milan in July 2024.

The partners struck up a romance in season five, but broke up a few months after their shocking exit. Still, Bryan and Ballas remained friendly, with The Cheetah Girls star even returning to the ballroom to cheer for him the following season.

Funnily enough, the duo had gone out on several dates before he even signed up for the show. And while they denied any romance rumors during season 18, that didn't stop them from playing up their chemistry during performances.

Soon after the Shark Tank star announced he was separating from his wife of 14 years Diane Plese, sources confirmed to E! News that he and Kym Johnson, his pro partner from season 20, were dating and "really happy together."

While Robert and Kym at first played coy about the nature of their relationship, that quickly stopped. They were engaged in February 2016, married by June 2016, and welcomed twins in April 2018.

Partnered in season three, the Saved by the Bell alum quickly struck up a romance with the dance pro, which went on for two years before they called it off for good in 2008. "The relationship wasn't heading in the right direction," Smirnoff's rep said in a statement, after rumors of infidelity on Lopez's part.

The professional dancers got engaged in 2009 after six months of dating following her split from Mario Lopez. Sadly, they called it off later that same year. But the duo remained friendly, even going on vacations together.

Married since 2014, the pros announced the arrival of their daughter Nikita in May 2023.

Daniella shared the happy news by posting a photo and video of Pasha with Nikita to Instagram Stories. She wrote "daddy's girl" alongside the clip and "My Geminis" beside the picture.

After showing off their insane chemistry during the sixth season, the duo dated for nearly a year before announcing their 2009 breakup in the most cordial way ever: matching tweets! "Hi everyone, we wanted you all to know directly from us, that Shannon & I have decided to end our relationship as boyfriend & girlfriend...," Hough tweeted that August, with Elizabeth writing, "However, we love and care about each other very much and will remain friends and in each others lives."

Derek is now married to his dance partner Hayley Erbert.

#750. Dubois vs Parker announced for WBO heavyweight title clash

Daniel Dubois will box former world champion Joseph Parker on January 30 at Manchester's Co-op Live arena; Dubois will be defending the WBO heavyweight world title he secured defeating Fabio Wardley; Parker has had his suspension lifted

Daniel Dubois will defend the WBO heavyweight world championship against Joseph Parker on January 30 at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.

Dubois and Parker were due to box in 2025 for the IBF title, only for Dubois to fall ill and withdraw just three days before the fight.

Parker knocked out short-notice replacement Martin Bakole and then lost a WBO Interim title bout to Fabio Wardley.

In August he announced that he could continue his career after a suspension was lifted following a failed drug test in October 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Dubois lost the IBF strap to Oleksandr Usyk last year but stormed back to form when he twice halted Wardley, winning and retaining the full WBO world championship.

He will now be back in action early in the new year against Parker, who's also recorded standout wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang in recent years.

A former holder of the belt, the New Zealander lost the WBO championship to Anthony Joshua back in 2018 at the Principality Stadium when he became the first professional opponent to go the distance with Joshua.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Frank Warren said: "This heavyweight showdown will deliver a blockbuster beginning to 2027.

"It's a fight everyone wanted to see, and I'm thrilled we can now make it happen. Daniel is entering his prime and when he is on his game it is hard to picture anybody beating him.

"But Joseph has long promised to become world champion again, and now he gets his chance."

#749. Hayden Panettiere’s Net Worth Revealed After Her Death

Three months after Hayden Panettiere died from an accidental overdose at the age of 36, court documents obtained by E! News revealed the net worth of the estate inherited by her daughter.

Hayden Panettiere’s daughter is inheriting her estate.

Just over three months after the Nashville star died from an accidental overdose at the age of 36, her 11-year-old daughter Kaya—who she shares with former fiancé Wladimir Klitschko—was named the sole heir to her estate, which is valued at $6,232,119.00, according to court documents obtained by E! News.

As Panettiere died without a will, the document noted she left behind $5,208,519 in personal property and $1,023,600 in real property, for a combined estate valued at $6,232,119.

Klitschko was appointed as the temporary guardian of his daughter’s estate, and filed a petition asking that tax and financial advisor Melissa Moskal Bencivenga be appointed as administrator of the estate, per the docs.

Following Panettiere’s death, Klitschko—who dated Panettiere off and on from 2009 to 2018—filed for temporary guardianship of Kaya, explaining in a Sept. 24 court filing obtained by E! News that it was “urgent and essential” he be appointed as his daughter’s guardian to ensure he had eligibility to file a probate petition for her estate.

“Without an immediate appointment for these purposes, there is a high probability that property belonging to Hayden's Estate may be lost, damaged or dissipated before a duly appointed personal representative can be in place to protect it,” the filing read. “This directly and adversely affects Kaya, as she is the sole heir entitled to the entirety of Hayden's probate estate.”

The former professional boxer said he also fronted $30,000 of his own money to cover Panettiere’s estimated taxes in October, stating in court docs that he wanted to prevent “unnecessary interest” and additional penalties, as well as avoid “direct financial detriment” to Kaya.

The 50-year-old noted in the docs that he would “later seek reimbursement” from the estate once it was set up.

In the years following her daughter’s birth, Panettiere was candid about the postpartum depression she suffered and her struggles with substance abuse, which ultimately led her to give full custody of Kaya to Klitschko in 2018.

"I was going through a really challenging time in my life,” the Bring It On: All of Nothing alum told Momé in July. “I knew I needed to be able to put her first so that I could get the help I needed and be the mom she needed me to be."

And once she was able to focus on herself, she and Kaya formed a much closer bond.

"I love my daughter, and I'm so proud of the young woman she is becoming,” she shared. “I talk to her all the time, and I feel so connected to her. She's like a mini-me."

Panettiere died on Aug. 16 while staying at an apartment in South Carolina, with the Greenville Police Department confirming on Oct. 28 that authorities had closed the investigation into her death, ruling it an accidental overdose.

The Greenville County Coroner's Office previously determined the Heroes alum died from "toxic effects" of fentanyl and four other substances.

To read more about the investigation into Panettiere's tragic passing, keep reading.

Hayden Panettiere died in Greenville, South Carolina, on Aug. 16. She was 36.

After receiving a 911 call at around 1:51 p.m. on Aug. 16, first responders and emergency medical services arrived at a residence in Greenville and found a woman—later identified as Panettiere—in cardiac arrest, according to a release shared by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office the following day. While "advanced cardiac life support measures" were provided, the release continued, the "resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful" as Panettiere was unresponsive. The actress was pronounced dead at the scene a little after 2:30 p.m.In audio of the emergency dispatch call obtained by CNN and TMZ, EMS responders could be heard discussing an apparent overdose. However, the official cause and manner of death were not initially revealed as the coroner's office and Greenville City Police Department continued their investigations.

What Was Hayden Panettiere's Cause of Death?

In its Aug. 17 release, the coroner's office confirmed an autopsy was completed and that "no signs of trauma were discovered that would have contributed to the death" of the Heroes star.About a month later, Panettiere's official cause of death was revealed."The cause of death has been ruled as toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol, and Quetiapine," the Greenville County Coroner's Office said in a statement Sept. 22. "The manner of death has been ruled accident."

Who Was With Hayden Panettiere When She Died?

The Greenville City Police Department noted in its Aug. 17 release that "an acquaintance of Ms. Panettiere placed the 911 call," with a redacted police report obtained by E! listing both Brian Hickerson—her on-again, off-again boyfriend since 2018— and his brother Zach Hickerson as the ones to call 911.Zach later told officers investigating Panettiere's death that she was Brian's girlfriend, according to Greenville City PD's report.Zach also shared in an Aug. 21 statement to TMZ that Brian gave Panettiere Narcan—an opioid overdose reversal medication—after the pair found the actress unconscious in the apartment she was renting. Zach also said that he and Brian "jointly performed CPR while 911 was on speaker until Fire and EMS arrived." Police noted in an Aug. 16 release that "the preliminary investigation has not indicated any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances" around her death.

How Did Brian Hickerson and Zach Hickerson React to Hayden Panettiere's Death?

In the police report, an officer noted Zach was "very emotional while EMS were working on" Panettiere, though "Brian did not become emotional until EMS declared her officially deceased."E! News has reached out to Zach for comment but has not heard back. Meanwhile, Brian's attorney Sloan Ellis has spoken out.

"Hayden's death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed," Ellis told E! News Aug. 20. "As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play. Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time."And while police told People officers "responded to a call for a welfare check at a home belonging to Brian Hickerson’s family" on Aug. 19, they noted "the call is unrelated to the Hayden Panettiere death investigation and did not require an incident report."

What Has Hayden Panettiere's Family Said About Her Death?

After Panettiere died, her father Skip Panettiere told ABC News she was "an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her—and to the millions who watched her onscreen."Two days later, her mother Lesley Vogel broke her silence.

"This person in her life that we have been trying to get rid of for quite some time was with her at her death," she told NBC News Aug. 18, "and that was Brian Hickerson."

While Panettiere—whose brother Jansen died in 2023 at age 28—and her mom had publicly spoken about their estrangement, Vogel remembered her daughter as "an amazingly talented person in so many departments.""I think young people who grow up in the entertainment industry—it is a struggle and it’s a very challenging industry," she added, "and it’s not unusual for them to sadly find the wrong path."Additionally, her ex Wladimir Klitschko addressed his "profound shock and grief" he and their daughter Kaya were facing in the wake of Panettiere's death. The Ukranian boxer further vowed to keep the Nashville alum's legacy alive in Kaya's memory.

#747. Mister Rogers' Son John Rogers Dead at 65

Fred Rogers' son John Rogers—who was raised by the creator and star of Mister Rogers' Neighborhood and wife Joanne Byrd—died at 65 years old, more than two decades after the late TV host.

Mister Rogers' neighborhood is in mourning.

Beloved TV host Fred Rogers' youngest son, John Rogers, died at 65 years old, his family confirmed to TMZ. His cause of death was not shared.

John was born in 1961 to the puppeteer—who made television history as America's neighbor on Mister Rogers' Neighborhood from 1968 to 2001—and his wife Joanne Byrd Rogers following the arrival of son James Byrd Rogers in 1959.

John appeared with his brother on the children's show during their childhood in Pittsburgh, Pa., but went on to live a life outside of the public eye, which included a move to Florida in his 30s. However, he has occasionally returned to the spotlight to celebrate his father's legacy following his 2003 death, such as accepting a star on the Pittsburgh Walk of Fame on Fred's behalf.

"How many people have said 'It's a beautiful day in the neighborhood?'" John quoted the series' iconic opening line at the event. "What an honor this is, firstly for my dad."

Though Fred's show ended in 2001, John noted how much his dad's impact lived on with new generations.

In his words, "It's hard to believe he's been gone since 2003. His memory and his work live on beyond belief."

And having grown up in the city where his dad became an ordained Presbyterian Minister, John felt endeared to return back home over the years, noting, "Pittsburgh sort of reminds me of him."

"I can't find nicer people than Pittsburgh, and that's why I visit here quite often," he continued. "It's a lot of Mister Rogers-type people that live here that really are caring and wonderful, loving people."

In addition to accepting the posthumous honor, John met with Tom Hanks on the set of the biopic about Fred's life,  A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood. The late 74-year-old's wife Joanne was closely involved in the making of the 2019 film, before her death two years later.

"We're happy about the movie. Thought it was wonderful. I thought Tom Hanks' portrayal of the movie was just fabulous,” John gushed on Fox and Friends in 2019. "And when I heard that Tom was going to do it, I said in baseball terms, well, that's a grand slam, home run."

#746. EA adds AI-generated John Motson to FC 27 video game

John Motson was a legendary football commentator who covered 10 World Cups, 10 European Championships and 29 FA Cup finals for BBC Sport

Football game EA Sports FC will feature the digitally recreated voice of the late commentator John Motson, Electronic Arts has exclusively told the BBC.

Motson, who died in 2023, was the main commentator for BBC Sport for decades - and performed the same role for the video game series during the 90s and 00s.

It is the first time the hit series, formerly known as Fifa, has featured a deceased commentator.

With the permission of his widow and his son, Motson's voice has been synthesised using a combination of old recording sessions and generative AI. It will become available in FC 27 on 26 November.

The legendary commentator died aged 77 in February 2023 - several months after the launch of ChatGPT and the massive growth of AI it set in train.

Fred Motson told the BBC it "means an awful lot" to have his dad's voice in EA Sports FC once again.

"I grew up with Fifa," he said. "I always used to tell my parents that I needed the latest console for Christmas because otherwise dad couldn't see how the game worked."

Electronic Arts, which was bought for $55bn (Â£42bn) in August, told the BBC it paid Motson's family for the rights to use his likeness and recreate his voice, but would not disclose the financial terms of the deal.

The BBC's lead football commentator Guy Mowbray said it was a "privilege" to be involved in the game, which he has provided commentary for since 2023.

"I think it's quite a nice, sort of non-scary use of AI," he said.

"We're in the business of nostalgia... I hear commentary not in my own voice, but in John's voice, because that's the voice I knew growing up.

"So I think it's nice that that legacy can be continued in this way."

WATCH: The new John Motson commentary in EA Sports FC 27 - and how it sounded back in Fifa 1998

John Motson was the first commentator for the series, appearing on games from Fifa 96 up to Fifa 2005. He later made a brief cameo in Fifa 19.

"While he completely understood when they went in a different direction, I think he really missed it after he left the game and it felt like a bit of an end of an era," his son said.

EA told the BBC the studio would not have included Motson in the game unless they had permission from his family.

"There was no way we would have moved forward with this in any way, shape or form if they weren't fully on board," said Mat Prior, senior game design director at EA Sports FC.

"At the outset we wanted to pay tribute to to Motty as the commentator and as this emotional connection - he was the very first voice of our game - so we really wanted to do him justice and bring him back."

He explained that Motson's voice in the game was a combination of old lines he recorded over the years and AI - tech which he said was "the only way" to make it happen, as they don't have recordings of him talking about modern players like Bradley Barcola and Chloe Kelly.

Gazza's tears, Radford's screamer & the Crazy Gang - 5 of Motty's best

Motson's son Fred said he believed his dad would have "absolutely" wanted to be involved in the game after his death.

"My dad was the least technological person in the world," he said. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk.

"So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically - but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects."

But Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now which campaigns against AI voice cloning, expressed some disquiet about the project, and the fact Motson had been unable to consent to it.

"If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he said.

"But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed.

"Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either."

One of the main arguments against the use of generative AI in video games is that it can replace humans - something that EA was keen to argue against.

"From a gaming standpoint, it's something we've used for many years - like machine learning to help drive animation systems and so on and so forth," Prior said.

"It's not there to replace commentators in any way shape or form... there's certainly no future plans to replace anyone with AI."

Derek Rae, who has been a commentator in EA FC for several years, said the tech could make things easier, but he still spent a long time recording dialogue in studios.

"It's quite a lot of days in the course of a year," he said. "So it might be two or three times a month that we do it in season for the game, which is typically sort of November time through until May.

"The more creative things have to be done with the human voice because they have to have the personality, sometimes a little chuckle thrown in the middle of a sentence or a little idiosyncrasy," he said.

"But when it comes to the more normal features in a video game, for example, routine surnames like Smith and Jones and Brown, that's something that AI can probably accomplish quite easily."

Josko Gvardiol tackling Jamal Musiala in FC 27 - perhaps examples of some less routine surnames

Rae said he was excited about the Motson project - but wasn't convinced he would follow suit.

"If we're being modest, we might say, well, no, I don't want to inflict my voice on the next generation."

He told BBC News it was something he would need to "think about" it but added: "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that."

#744. A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

The latest HIV-vaccine strategies aim to trigger the development of antibodies that can prevent infection by a range of HIV strains. Credit: 3DMedisphere/SPL

In the mid-2000s, a young woman in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa became infected with HIV. Her story could have represented just another sobering statistic in the epidemic that was tearing through the region, but instead, she became a source of inspiration for scientists and of hope for millions. Enrolled in a study to track the course of newly acquired infections, the woman mounted a ferocious immune response to the virus over the next several years as doctors in the study treated her and took regular blood samples to monitor what was going on in her body.

Although she could not control the virus without the help of drugs, the antibodies she raised against HIV are recognized as among the strongest that have ever been discovered1. The woman is known in the literature as CAP256.

Scientists now think that by mimicking some of the key elements of an infection like hers, they might be able to train other people’s immune systems to make similarly potent antibodies that can block a diverse array of HIV strains. Ultimately, they say, they might achieve one of the most elusive goals in biomedical research: a vaccine that can stop HIV in its tracks.

The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

“We have a line of sight to an efficacious vaccine,” says Mark Feinberg, president and chief executive of the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative (IAVI) in New York City. “The scientific promise is greater than it’s ever been.”

This year, several teams described vaccination strategies that — in monkeys — can trigger the production of what are known as broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs), molecules that can completely shut down an infection from a diverse range of HIV strains before it begins2–4. “No one has achieved that before. It’s a very important milestone,” says Rogier Sanders, a virologist at Amsterdam University Medical Centre.

Humans who have received components of similar vaccines can produce precursors to these bnAbs5–7, suggesting that with further refinement, an effective vaccine is possible.

Success is by no means guaranteed, says Feinberg. HIV has proved a formidable foe for vaccine developers in the past. And there is another factor that adds complications. The availability of successful drugs, such as lenacapavir, that prevent HIV infection might make it difficult to test how well a vaccine works. Meanwhile, devastating cuts to the US funding that supported preclinical and clinical research for HIV have left some efforts on a precipice.

“We’re in a better position than we’ve ever been, and just at this time, we’ve seen the funding streams cut off,” says Dennis Burton, an immunologist and virologist at Scripps Research, a research institute in La Jolla, California.

The latest glimmers of success follow decades of failure. Initially, scientists looking to develop an HIV vaccine followed a strategy that had been successful for many other viruses, including hepatitis B: administer a lab-made version of the proteins that viruses use to attach to host cells and the body should start producing antibodies that will block infection. In HIV’s case, it’s the surface protein known as envelope that latches onto a molecular receptor on human T cells so that the virus can infect them. “There was only one protein, and so it seemed straightforward,” says Sallie Permar, a vaccinologist and paediatrician at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York City.

Starting in the 1980s, researchers made vaccines that contained the HIV envelope protein, to elicit antibodies against it, but the vaccines failed to prevent infection in clinical-trial participants. HIV mutates rapidly and most circulating strains were still able to mount an infection. “With HIV, there are millions of strains circulating simultaneously. Taking out one does nothing,” says Richard Wyatt, a viral immunologist at Scripps Research.

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Researchers tried other strategies, such as vaccines that recruited ‘killer’ T cells to wipe out infected cells, and those that delivered a wider diversity of proteins to overcome HIV’s penchant for mutation. In 2009, a clinical trial in Thailand reported modest signs of protection for a vaccine that triggered both T-cell and antibody responses8. But efforts to replicate those results failed, and that strategy was abandoned, too.

One overarching problem, says Feinberg, was that nobody knew what the immunological signature — the measurable biological response after injection — of an effective HIV vaccine looked like, so the only way to assess a candidate was to conduct large-scale efficacy trials and hope for the best. “It was all a shot in the dark,” says Burton.

That attitude began to change after the discovery of bnAbs. In the 1990s, teams led by Burton and microbiologist Hermann Katinger, then at the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences in Vienna, identified the first of them in individuals who were living with HIV9,10. These bnAbs could protect monkeys from infection by HIV strains circulating in Europe and America, but it took large doses, which were unlikely to be reached and sustained with a vaccine. And the protection was less effective against some strains from Africa.

In the 2000s, Burton’s team developed a way to sort through vast numbers of B cells — the immune cells that produce antibodies — for the rare ones that make bnAbs. After screening around 1,800 people living with HIV, they identified a pair of highly potent bnAbs, made by a donor in Africa, that blocked infection from dozens of HIV strains11. “That ignited the field,” says Burton.

Researchers would have to learn how to train the immune system to produce these kinds of bnAb. The strategies to do so emerged from the recognition that bnAbs often develop gradually in HIV-infected individuals such as CAP256. It happens through a sustained “cat and mouse game” between the fast-changing virus and an immune system struggling to keep up, says Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Diseases and the University of Witwatersrand, both in Johannesburg, who analysed CAP256’s blood.

To mimic that struggle in an uninfected person, researchers first deliver a ‘priming’ immunogen — a portion or complete copy of HIV’s envelope. This shot awakens B cells, triggering them to divide and become active. Subsequent doses deliver distinct versions of the HIV envelope to first ‘shape’ and then ‘polish’ the antibodies produced. The goal is to guide the awakened B cells through a process called affinity maturation, in which the antibodies develop extensive mutations that improve their binding and breadth. The key is that the most capable B cells are recruited early and the antibodies that they produce are honed over time (see ‘Targeted vaccines’).

Source: P. J. Klasse et al. Nature Rev. Microbiol. 23, 734–752 (2025).

Sanders says that this strategy, sometimes known as germline targeting, is a bit like looking for an elite footballer among pools of youth players. Rather than trying to train everyone up to an expert level, they want to identify talent early and nurture it to superstardom. “We’re scouting the talented B cells,” Sanders says.

Researchers have taken different approaches to scouting these cells. After Moore and colleagues discovered CAP256’s antibodies, they sequenced the viruses circulating in her blood to identify what might have triggered and shaped the antibodies’ production.

A modified version of the envelope protein from one such virus has shown promise as a priming agent for the immune system in monkeys and is now being trialled in humans, says virologist George Shaw who co-led the preclinical work for this2 with virologist Beatrice Hahn, both at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia.

Another team, led by William Schief at Scripps Research, used computational structural modelling and cell studies to design immunogens that activate a specific subset of B cells that make antibodies capable of blocking the binding site through which HIV latches onto T cells5.

Trump team guts AIDS-eradication programme and slashes HIV research grants

Trump team guts AIDS-eradication programme and slashes HIV research grants

In small trials of vaccination with either protein or mRNA-based versions of this immunogen12, which is called eOD-GT8, nearly all participants developed ‘bnAb precursors’. These are antibodies with the desired genetic and structural characteristics of a bnAb that blocks the T-cell binding site on the envelope protein, but not the bevy of mutations that makes bnAbs elite. In participants who also got a booster shot of a different immunogen, the antibodies picked up mutations that improved their binding and neutralization abilities. “It worked beautifully,” says Schief, who is also vice-president for protein design at Moderna Therapeutics in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

#743. 'Justice for sport' - Afcon reaction as Senegal reinstated as winners

Senegal's football federation reacted to the Cas verdict on social media with a picture of the side lifting the Afcon trophy alongside the caption "again and always champions of Africa"

That was the initial reaction of Senegal football federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall to the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate the West Africans as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions.

The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final but were stripped of the title in March by a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board, which imposed a 3-0 forfeit after they walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded against them when the game was goalless.

Following a hearing in Lausanne in October, a three-man Cas panel unanimously overturned that ruling by Caf, effectively judging that the decisions taken by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala in restarting the match and playing it to a conclusion were final.

Morocco's football federation (FRMF), however, says it will "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision".

The North Africans could yet take their fight to the Swiss Federal Court.

Those in Senegal have celebrated the return of the title, while several legal experts have backed the Cas verdict.

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling

Senegal's talisman Sadio Mane, who was named player of the tournament at Afcon 2025, said the ruling "fills us with joy".

The 34-year-old former Liverpool man thanked his team-mates and Senegal staff as well as the whole Senegalese nation at home and abroad.

"Your faith in us gave us strength during the most difficult moments. This victory is yours, too," he said in a statement on social media.

Senegal captain Kalidou Koulibaly, who missed the final through injury, echoed that sentiment.

"Some victories are won on the pitch, while others are won in the heart of a people," he said in a post on Facebook.

"Long before this verdict, there was you - your prayers, your flags in the windows, your fervour, and the pride that unites us all: the pride of the people of Teranga."

Pape Gueye, the man who scored the extra-time winner in Rabat, described the Cas decision as "an immense relief".

Both he and Mane had a message of support for Morocco.

"Senegal and Morocco are brotherly nations; may our shared passion for football continue to bring us closer together," Mane said.

Gueye added: "Beyond football, the respect and fraternity between our two peoples remain what matters most. Let's hold on to that.

Afcon: Is the Senegal v Morocco saga finally over?

Morocco's main complaint is that Articles 82 and 84 of Afcon tournament regulations - which were implemented by the Caf appeals board in March - were not followed by Cas.

Article 82 states that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" it shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

Article 84 then states a 3-0 forfeit should be imposed on a team which is eliminated in such circumstances.

"There [are] football rules that should have been applied by the referee," former Morocco international Hassan Kachloul told BBC Sport.

"When the Senegalese players left the pitch, the game should have been over."

The FRMF registered its "surprise" at the Cas decision and said that the panel "failed to account for the stance recently established" by the International Football Association Board (Ifab), the game's ultimate lawmakers, and world governing body Fifa regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee's permission.

However, Ifab only updated its laws in April - three months after the Afcon final - to state that a referee may send off any player who leaves the field when protesting a decision.

Moroccan football journalist Jalal Bounouar says his compatriots are "frustrated and disappointed" by the ruling.

"The main reason is that Caf's appeal board had already applied Article 82 and 84 of the competition regulations which considered Senegal to have forfeited the match," he told Newsday on the BBC World Service.

"Many Moroccans feel the decision by Cas has ignored the importance of these rules. From the Moroccan perspective, the referee should have taken stronger disciplinary action.

"We feel that our team was put in a difficult situation and that the final was not managed fairly."

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 champions - ten months on

Cas has a long-standing practice of following what has been called the 'field of play' doctrine.

It refrains from "reviewing decisions taken on the playing field by referees for applying the rules of the game, unless there is evidence that those rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith".

"The primary argument was that the referee is the master of the decision on the pitch," said Serge Vittoz, a member of the FSF's legal team.

Raymond Hack, both a former head of disciplinary at Caf and a former arbiter at Cas, said the judgement was the "correct verdict".

"What everyone seems to forget - and whilst there may be contradictory information in Article 82 and 84 - decisions taken by the referee during the match are final," the South African told the BBC World Service.

"Only the referee can start a game. Only a referee can end a game."

For former Nigeria striker Daniel Amokachi, an Afcon winner in 1994, the Cas ruling is "the right decision".

"At the end of the day, the man in charge of the match (Ndala) restarted the game, the game ended," he said.

Caf president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said his organisation will respect and adhere to Cas' decision

Caf has already tightened its own regulations to avoid a repeat.

But Algerian sports journalist Maher Mezahi says the continental governing body still needs to salvage its image.

"How many times have we seen Caf's legal institutions, whether it be the disciplinary board or the appeals committee, come up with these decisions that we all find ridiculous," he said.

"They end up being challenged at Cas and eventually they get overturned.

"We have to rebuild trust in Caf's own judicial bodies because it is a little bit humiliating and degrading and it brings the entire reputation of the confederation into disrepute."

The 2027 Afcon is scheduled to take place in June and July next year, and Senegal and Morocco were among the first qualifiers earlier this month.

Kachloul says the next tournament provides a chance to draw a definitive line under what happened in Rabat in January.

"This event, wherever you look at it on the Senegalese side or Moroccan side, doesn't look good at all," the one-time Aston Villa midfielder said.

"They are lucky to have another [Afcon] tournament in six months to redeem themselves and to paint a better picture of African football.

"The best way to prove that you're the best is to go back on the pitch and let the football talk."

#742. Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut

The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.

Stay tuned for more on these stories and anything else in or concerning Germany on November 16, 2026.

We'll be back with the latest headlines out of Germany tomorrow. Bis dann!

Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

Germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

Speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — said: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half."

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

"We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team."

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, have entered talks over a scheme to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

The plan to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been announced by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had first been announced back in September.

Tesla has earmarked some €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory in Germany, near to Berlin.

The Grünheide complex will be expanded to start producing the electric car company's driverless Cybercabs, with output expected to eventually reach 1 million units.

The Elon Musk-owned company said construction would begin in 2027, with the first Cybercabs rolling off the line in 2029.

"With this, we are laying the foundations for the world's most technologically advanced Tesla factory here in Grünheide," Tesla said.

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

Matt Pearson on our sports desk breaks down where the power struggle currently stands, with the deadline for candiates just a matter of hours away now.

Lawmakers in the state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have voted in Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier.

The 52-year-old has been in the role since 2017 and is heading into a third term.

The vote was a secret ballot, but it can still be assumed who voted and how.

She received 39 of the 68 votes cast in the chamber, exactly as many as commanded by Schwesig's three-party coaliton of her Social Democrats (29), the ecologist Greens (5), and the socialist Left Party (5).

While Söder's comments in Munich focused in particular on the policy the coalition in Berlin had not delivered, Merz initiatlly focused on talking up the efficacy of his federal coalition.

"We are aware of the situation. We know that we now need to deliver. And we also know that we face difficult talks within the coalition. But I would also say from the experiences of the last weeks that there are solutions to the problems which we have in Germany," Merz said.

Merz said that in the 18 months since last year's election, the coalition "has already successfully implemented many things, not 'set them into motion' as people like to say, but actually implemented."

He noted a total of 17 bills going through the second and third reading process in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, last week, "including the most comprehensive reforms of our intelligence and security services that we have ever done in [post-war] Germany."

Among others, he thanked Bavarian Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a senior member of the Bavarian CSU sister party to Merz's own conservative CDU, for his contribution to this.

Merz also touted the support given to CSU politician Ilse Aigner, not just from his CDU but from the Social Democrat coalition partners and the Greens, to become the next president, calling her a person who would "represent our country very well at home and abroad."

After hailing these accomplishments, Merz then turned to electricity tax cuts, saying he anticipated talks on the matter on Tuesday that would be "very short."

He said that over the weekend, coalition leaders had revisited the figures, and now believed they would be able to "completely" reduce electricity taxes to the minimum European levels in 2027 "also for private households."

Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has appeared with Friedrich Merz at a press conference during the chancellor's trip to Munich.

It seems Söder, Merz and the CDU/CSU believe they have unfinished business after the budget was finalized in the Bundestag late last week.

Merz had pledged in the run-up to the decision to provide a reduction in electricity tax for all, but the final agreement did not include this step, with the coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) saying it was not adequately costed.

Söder said he and Merz had discussed "backup for the coming days," for Berlin and for a "collective stance, that is really, really important."

He said the coming days were about "demonstrating credibility in politics," seemingly in reference to Merz's promise that the coalition did not ultimately deliver.

"That's why it's really important to us that we do indeed bring about the reduction in electricity tax," Söder said. "This is important for businesses. It would be a relief for citizens. But it's also a matter of credibility and it's written in the coalition agreement."

Söder said that as to the question of "where the money comes from, with a €560 billion (roughly $615 billion) budget, with €200 billion in new debt, nobody can tell me there's no potential within the budgeting process."

A festive piece of merchandise on the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) "fan shop" website has upset some religious leaders in Germany.

Called a "chocolate Nicholas," it appears to depict a semblance of Saint Nicholas in bishop's regalia and the party's colors and holding a book with "AfD" written on the cover where a Bible might be in more traditional iconography.

The Bishop of Essen, Franz-Josef Overbeck, was highly critical of the promotion in Monday's edition of the Bild newspaper.

"The AfD is appropriating Christian symbols for party campaigning," Overbeck said. "Showing the holy Nicholas in a blue coat with mitre, staff and the gospel with an AfD logo is not in order."

Overbeck acknowledged that other organizations like football clubs would sell chocolate Christmas figurines in club colors, but he said they would tend to refrain from including overtly Christian symbols when doing so.

Bild quoted an AfD spokesman as saying that as a "liberal-conservative party that clearly associates itself with Christian values," the item fit "particularly well" with the party image.

The main German protestant church group EKD's cultural representative, Johann Hinrich Claussen, said the offer showed the AfD had "no understanding of traditions and no respect" for Christianity.

He described the action as "embarrassing and revealing," and said that Christianity was "supra-partisan."

"The AfD knows little about what is holy to Christians. Otherwise, it would be aware that Bishop Nicholas of Myra, in what today is Demre in Turkey, stood clearly for uniting the occident and the orient. Beyond that, he is the patron saint of rescues at sea," Claussen said.

The partner of deceased Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger has said that anybody is welcome at his funeral this coming Saturday.

Aiwanger was the economy minister in Bavaria's state government as the leader of the junior coalition partners to the center-right CSU.

"Hubert was a man of the people and so it stands to reason that anyone who liked or treaasured him is allowed to come to his funeral," Tanja Schweiger wrote on her Instagram profile overnight.

She was posting after a requiem in the state capital Munich paying tribute to the leader of the Free Voters (Freie Wähler) party over the weekend. Around 1,100 people attended this ceremony.

Aiwanger died suddenly and unexpectedly on November 4 during a working visit to Berlin, aged 55.

Prosecutors have since said he died of natural causes, after he was found dead in his hotel room.

Germany's national men's football team will play neighbors and rivals the Netherlands for the 50th time on Monday night.

And there's quite a lot at stake for Jürgen Klopp's team in the last group stage game of the Nations League competition at Berlin's Olympiastadion.

If Germany win, they will qualify for the knockout stages, but a defeat could lead to potential relegation into the second tier of Nations League football.

Klopp was upbeat in the pre-match press conference at the prospect of playing the Netherlands, who he said play "Xavi football," in the image of the skillful Spanish playmaker and World Cup winner coaching the team.

"I've always loved playing against teams like this. For all my coaching career," Klopp said. "When someone says, 'hey they can really play football,' then in my mind the party's already started."

A full house with some 71,000 fans is expected in the capital when the game kicks off. Klopp played on the Dutch reputation for liberal use of bicylces in his comments to reporters, saying he wanted to "put a stick in their spokes" and dislodge them from the saddle.

The notion of a bridge over the valley between Ratingen and Heiligenhaus to the east of Düsseldorf in western Germany as part of the A44 highway is more than half a century old. And the physical bridge itself has stood, complete, ever since 2022.

Yet still the crossing is not connected to any roads at either end.

A construction project to build the last 4.4 kilometers of highway and link the bridge to the A44 highway will formally start on Monday.

State premier Hendrik Wüst, as well as the regional transport and traffic ministers will attend the ground-breaking ceremony.

A project first conceived some 55 years ago has faced repeated delays because of lawsuits, environmental protection studies and onerous planning and permit procedures.

The bridge across the Angerbachtal (Angerbach Valley) should improve the road connection between the North Rhine-Westphalia state capital of Düsseldorf, the Bergisches Land mountain range and the industrial cities in the Ruhr Valley. It's also meant to help remove some strain from the perenially busy A3 highway and to improve the road connections to Düsseldorf International Airport.

The last stretch of highway is expected to cost around €200 million (roughly $220 million), or roughly the annual costs incurred each year by forcing traffic to divert around it, according to estimates from Düsseldorf's IHK industry and trade association.

Construction is expected to take several years, no formal end date has yet been set.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz heads to Munich early on Monday, for a meeting with the leadership of the Bavarian Christian Social Democrats (CSU), the sister party to his conservative  Christian Democrats(CDU).

No concrete details about the talks were made public ahead of time, except for the CSU saying it would serve as a general exchange that had been planned for some time.

The trip comes a week after Merz nominated Ilse Aigner as the next German president, likely paving the way for her to become the first woman and first CSU politician to assume the role.

It also follows soon after the 2027 federal budget cleared a marathon meeting of the parliamentary budget committee in Berlin. This serves as one of the more conspicuous examples of the frictions and difficulties in the grand coalition between the Christian Democrats and the center-left Social Democrats — with the compromises it contains a point of frustration among the CSU and for state premier Markus Söder.

The northeastern state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania will likely vote in Social Democrat (SPD) Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier early in the afternoon.

The 52-year-old, who first stepped into the role in 2017, plans to lead a new coalition of the SPD, the environmentalist Greens and the socialist Left Party after state elections in September.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest single party in the sparsely populated state.

But still, the political calculus that emerged was arguably simpler than in Berlin — where the socialist Left Party is the largest party but could struggle to lead a coaltion — and in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD was by far the largest party but short of an outright majority.

Schwesig's SPD claimed 29 seats, with the Greens and the Left each taking 5, meaning that when combined, they hold a fairly clear majority over the AfD with its 32 seats.

The SPD's relatively successful performance in the state, at least compared to its national struggles, has also led to Schwesig being linked with a possible return to federal politics. The SPD plans to elect a new leadership duo early next year.

Schwesig has already had a spell in Berlin as the federal minsiter for families, pensioners and women, and briefly led the SPD on an interim basis in 2017, but after this she returned to her home state to seek the top regional job instead.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Servus! Welcome to another Monday of news and analysis of matters making waves in German politics and society.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz is starting his week in Munich, at a meeting of the Bavarian CSU sister party to his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU).

This comes a few days after Merz naming CSU politician Ilse Aigner as candidate to be the next president, and days after the budget committee signed off on the federal government's spending plans for 2027. Merz is expected to appear with state premier Markus Söder in a joint press conference later.

Far to the north, in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Social Democrat Manuela Schwesig should be voted in for another term as state premier in the regional parliament later in the day. Schwesig emerged in pole position after state elections a few weeks ago; some suspect her regional success could translate into national ambitions within the struggling party.

And in the west, regional leaders are headed to a road to nowhere — literally, but also hopefully not for very much longer now.

The vast highway A44 bridge over the valley between Helsinghausen and Ratingen-Ost has been planned for decades, and was completed in 2022, but work to actually connect it to the road network will only start today.

Stay with us for more on these stories and whatever else develops around Germany on November 16.
